claim: Jiang, Li and Wang decompose each trading day into 15-minute intraday intervals between 9:45am and 4:00pm plus one overnight interval from the previous day's 4:00pm close to the current day's 9:45am price (using the 9:45 price so most stocks have traded at least once after the open), and reclassify raw TAQ prices with CRSP's split/dividend adjustment factors before computing returns.
quote: we then compute intraday returns as every 15-minute return between 9:45 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. and the overnight return as the return between 4:00 p.m. on the previous trading day and 9:45 a.m. on the current trading day
limitations: This is the 2019-08-06 working-paper draft (title "News Momentum"), read via direct PDF page rendering (fetch tooling could not extract machine text from this PDF), transcribed by hand from the pages actually viewed; the published JFE 2021 version ("Pervasive underreaction...") may differ in wording, though the construction, sample, and headline numbers match what Hao Jiang's own CV and the SSRN/crossref bibliographic record report for the published paper.
impact_on_spec: Pins the exact M=26 interval grid (1 overnight + 25 intraday 15-minute intervals) that scripts/build_news_hf_reaction.py replicates on 1-minute SIP bars in place of TAQ ticks.

claim: For news occurring within regular trading hours the news return is the 15-minute return of the interval the news occurs in; for news during the weekend, a holiday, or overnight, the news return is instead the nearest subsequent overnight interval -- e.g. weekend news gets the Friday-4pm-to-Monday-9:45am return.
quote: For news occurring during the weekend, holiday, or overnight, the news return is the nearest subsequent overnight return to reflect that the first reaction to such news stories is incorporated into the stock's price only for the first trade of the following trading day.
impact_on_spec: Pins scripts/build_news_hf_reaction.py's attribute_news() rule: regular-hours news attributes to the same session's intraday bucket, everything else (pre-9:45, post-16:00, weekend, holiday) attributes to the next session's overnight bucket.

claim: At the 4:00pm close of each day, stocks are sorted into equal-weighted decile portfolios on that day's news return; a self-financing long-top-decile/short-bottom-decile strategy held one week (overlapping cohorts, Jegadeesh-Titman 1993 style) averaged -0.78%/month (decile 1) to +2.55%/month (decile 10), a 3.34%/month spread (t=11.72), ~40%/yr, Sharpe ~3.29, over March 2000-October 2012.
quote: The average monthly return increases from -0.78% for the loser portfolio in decile 1 to 2.55% for the winner portfolio in decile 10, yielding a return of 3.34% per month with a t-statistic of 11.72.
limitations: Gross-of-cost, long-short, 2000-2012 sample; this draft does not itself state a transaction-cost scenario -- see direction-review.json remaining_evidence_gap for the unverified 18bp/1.37%-net figure the registry carries from elsewhere.
impact_on_spec: The reported magnitude and its long-short structure are why the signal-card admission rule tests the long leg (rank direction +1) rather than assuming symmetry with the short leg.

claim: The paper's own overnight-news event study states overnight news (which its intraday-hours grid cannot directly capture) constitutes more than half of the full news sample, and finds delayed (not immediate) reaction to it.
quote: Using an intraday event study approach, we find compelling evidence for delayed reaction to overnight news, which constitutes more than half of our sample.
limitations: Same draft-vs-published caveat; corroborated independently by our own local data fact (57.1% of our 2024+ Alpaca/Benzinga news items arrive outside 09:30-16:00 ET), see data-feasibility.json.
impact_on_spec: Justifies why scripts/build_news_hf_reaction.py's overnight-bucket handling is not a minor edge case -- it is more than half of the data on both the paper's sample and ours.

claim: Crossref's bibliographic record for SSRN DOI 10.2139/ssrn.2679614 confirms the paper "Pervasive underreaction: Evidence from high-frequency data" by Hao Jiang, Sophia Zhengzi Li and Hao Wang, with an abstract matching the Duke working-paper draft's own abstract -- i.e. the SSRN-listed/published paper and the working-paper draft actually read are the same paper.
quote: We propose a novel high-frequency decomposition of daily stock returns into news- and non-news-driven components, and uncover evidence of pervasive stock market underreaction to firm news.
limitations: Crossref's "posted" date (2015-10-28) is the SSRN posting timestamp, not the 2019 working-paper draft date or the 2021 JFE publication date; this record is a bibliographic/abstract match only, not the full paper text (SSRN and ScienceDirect both blocked direct fetch this pass, 403).
impact_on_spec: Confirms the Duke-hosted working-paper draft (jlw_construction_* claims) and the JFE-published "Pervasive underreaction" paper the registry direction cites are the same underlying work, not two different papers.
